summary: The Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act aims to promote the global export and adoption of United States artificial intelligence systems, computing hardware, cloud services, and technical standards to allies and partners. The bill directs federal departments, primarily Commerce and State, to create programs that facilitate these exports, reduce foreign trade barriers, establish security measures to prevent access by foreign adversaries, study global AI deployment, and track export success over time.

affected_groups.effect: Must establish an export promotion program for industry consortia, work on security measures with foreign purchasers, develop confidence standards, and complete biannual export success trackers and reports.
Must work to eliminate foreign barriers, establish a diplomatic strategy, and coordinate studies on the global deployment of artificial intelligence.
Eligible to submit proposals through industry consortia to export the U.S. full AI stack, benefit from reduced foreign barriers, and utilize a new industry communications hotline.
affected_groups.group: United States AI Industry and Consortia

affected_groups.effect: Collaborate with U.S. agencies to adopt the U.S. full AI stack and institute security measures to block foreign adversary access.

key_provisions: Requires the Department of Commerce to establish a program to identify and receive proposals from industry consortia for exporting the U.S. full AI stack to allies and partners.

Requires the Department of Commerce, along with other agencies, to work with foreign purchasers to institute security measures preventing illicit or unauthorized foreign adversary access to the U.S. full AI stack.
Directs the Department of State to increase efforts to eliminate foreign barriers to exporting the U.S. full AI stack, including creating an industry hotline and holding listening sessions.
Requires the Secretary of State to establish a diplomatic strategy outlining how the U.S. will ease market access and communicate the benefits of using the U.S. full AI stack to foreign countries.

Mandates a study by the Department of State, Director of National Intelligence, and Department of Commerce on the benefits and impacts of the global deployment of AI, with a report due to congressional committees.
Requires the Department of Commerce to develop practices and standards to demonstrate confidence in the privacy, security, and effectiveness of the U.S. full AI stack to major foreign purchasers.

Requires the Department of Commerce to complete a biannual 'AI export success tracker' estimate for five years measuring global computing capacity, memory bandwidth, integrated circuits, data center ownership, model usage, and cloud revenue tied to U.S. firms.
missing_information: Specific funding levels or appropriations authorized to carry out the export programs and studies.
Exact penalties or enforcement mechanisms for foreign purchasers who violate security measures regarding adversary access.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act aims to promote the global export and adoption of United States artificial intelligence systems, computing hardware, cloud services, and technical standards to allies and partners. The bill directs federal departments, primarily Commerce and State, to create programs that facilitate these exports, reduce foreign trade barriers, establish security measures to prevent access by foreign adversaries, study global AI deployment, and track export success over time.
summary_detail.significance: The legislation addresses international technological competition and national security by seeking to establish U.S. artificial intelligence infrastructure, semiconductors, and standards as the global benchmark, while systematically restricting foreign adversaries from accessing these technologies.
